 Live scores | Today’s Football Daily | And email Scott 
 LIVE  Updated  44s ago Scott Murray Tue 17 Nov 2026 16.05 EST First published on Tue 17 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 30m ago HALF TIME: Wales 2-2 Portgual 
 37m ago GOAL! Wales 2-2 Portugal (Neto 43) 
 39m ago GOAL! Wales 2-1 Portugal (Thomas 40) 
 1h ago GOAL! Wales 1-1 Portugal (Brooks 13) 
 1h ago GOAL! Wales 0-1 Portugal (Fernandes 11) 
 3h ago The teams 
 3h ago Preamble 
 Portugal’s Pedro Neto finds the net to restore parity. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA View image in fullscreen Portugal’s Pedro Neto finds the net to restore parity. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Scott Murray Tue 17 Nov 2026 16.05 EST First published on Tue 17 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 30m ago HALF TIME: Wales 2-2 Portgual 
 37m ago GOAL! Wales 2-2 Portugal (Neto 43) 
 39m ago GOAL! Wales 2-1 Portugal (Thomas 40) 
 1h ago GOAL! Wales 1-1 Portugal (Brooks 13) 
 1h ago GOAL! Wales 0-1 Portugal (Fernandes 11) 
 3h ago The teams 
 3h ago Preamble 
 now 16.05 EST 61 min: Wilson has another go at finding the top-left corner with a curler from distance. High and wide again, but not by much.
 Share 1m ago 16.05 EST 60 min: Portugal make a double change, replacing Ramos and Trincão with João Félix and Carlos ‘CF7’ Forbs.
 Share 2m ago 16.04 EST 59 min: Pedro Neto turns on the jets to blaze past three red shirts down the inside-right channel. He reaches the Wales area and lashes a low drive across Ward and off the base of the left-hand post. So close to a sensational solo effort!
 Share 3m ago 16.02 EST 58 min: Wilson grooves into space down the inside-right channel and takes aim for the top left. Always going over, but close enough to get big portions of the crowd going.
 Share 5m ago 16.00 EST 56 min: Colwill dinks a pass down the left touchline to release Thomas into acres. Thomas reaches the edge of the box and rolls infield for James, who aims a curler intended for the bottom-left corner. Dalot blocks. Thomas is having a lot of joy on this left wing.
 Share 7m ago 15.59 EST 55 min: More of the Portuguese patience.
 Share 9m ago 15.57 EST 53 min: Trincão goes into the book for a cynical tug on the shirt of James.
 Share 9m ago 15.56 EST 51 min: Ramos advances down the left and is crudely stopped in his tracks by Cabango, who hasn’t taken long to go into the book. That was clumsy, and Ramos was lucky Cabango didn’t connect knee on fruitbowl. Nothing comes of the resulting free kick.
 Share Updated at  15.57 EST 11m ago 15.55 EST 50 min: Fernandes elegantly spins into space down the left but can’t find Ramos on the penalty spot. Wales nearly opened up there.
 Share 12m ago 15.53 EST 49 min: It’s all Portugal in terms of possession. Again. They’re pinging the ball around with a bit more pace, in the manner of a team who have been given the half-time what-for.
 Share 14m ago 15.51 EST 47 min: Fernandes cuts the corner back up the right touchline … nowhere near any of his team-mates. Very strange, and that’s released the pressure on Wales in extremely embarrassing fashion. The home fans enjoyed that.
 Share 15m ago 15.50 EST 46 min: Colwill is dispossessed a tad too easily and Portugal flow forward. Neto wins a corner off Sheehan. Fernandes to take from the right.
 Share 17m ago 15.49 EST Portugal get the second half started. Wales have made one change: Cabango is on for Rodon, reportedly a precautionary measure.
 Share 22m ago 15.44 EST Half-time entertainment. Wales fans! Get your Joe Jordan-infused schadenfreude here …
 Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable | Ewan Murray Read more … but we’re a broad church at Guardian sport, and we want Scotland fans to have something enjoyable to read too.
 Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes Read more Share 26m ago 15.39 EST Meanwhile in the other game in A4, it’s a half-time score of Denmark 2-1 Norway. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg and Rasmus Højlund put the hosts two up in short order in Copenhagen, but Erling Haaland scored his 67th goal for Norway on his 61st appearance to reduce the arrears. As things stand, this group will end Portugal , Denmark, Norway, Wales.
 Share 30m ago 15.36 EST HALF TIME: Wales 2-2 Portgual
 … nothing occurs. Turns out we did have enough added time for a goal or two, though. Both teams came so close. This is great.
 Share 31m ago 15.35 EST 45 min +3: … and now Wilson comes again, cutting in from the right and curling towards the bottom left. Costa is forced to turn around for a corner. From which …
 Share 31m ago 15.34 EST 45 min +2: So here’s the first half in microcosm. Rodon is skinned by Dalot down the left. Ramos meets the cross with a diving header that Davies bravely blocks with his trouser arrangement. The ball breaks to Wilson in the centre circle. Wilson spots Costa out of his box and goes for goal. His long-range rake beats Costa, but just clears the crossbar and lands on the top of the net! So close to an all-timer!
 Share 35m ago 15.31 EST 45 min +1: Portugal pass it around patiently and professionally, the spoilsports.
 Share 35m ago 15.30 EST 45 min: There will be two additional minutes. Plenty of time for another goal each.
 Share 37m ago 15.29 EST GOAL! Wales 2-2 Portugal (Neto 43)
 Trincão dribbles purposefully down the left and crosses long. The ball sails over Dasilva, and Neto can’t miss when the ball drops to him, a couple of yards out. Bing bong.
 View image in fullscreen Portugal’s Pedro Neto finds the net to restore parity. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto (right) is congratulated by a teammate after levelling the score. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.36 EST 38m ago 15.27 EST 42 min: Portugal should have gone 2-1 up; instead they’re now 2-1 down. This is fun.
 Share 39m ago 15.27 EST GOAL! Wales 2-1 Portugal (Thomas 40)
 Neto dribbles in from the right. He tees up Neves on the penalty spot. Neves shoots. Blocked. Ward claims. Wales counter immediately, and Thomas is sent racing into space down the inside-left channel. He enters the box, steps across the line of Neto so the Portugal man can’t make a tackle or intercept, opens his body, and steers into the bottom right! Bing bong!
 View image in fullscreen Sorba Thomas slots the ball home to give Wales the lead. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Thomas is joined by Harry Wilson (top) in the celebrations. Photograph: David Davies/PA Share Updated at  15.30 EST 41m ago 15.24 EST 39 min: Fernandes breaks into the box down the left and whips a low cross through the Wales six-yard box. Ramos hasn’t made the run, so Fernandes has his say. To be fair to Ramos, he was in danger of being caught offside in the build-up, so he’s got an excuse for having checked his forward movement.
 Share 44m ago 15.22 EST 37 min: Neto scuttles in from the right wing, reaches the edge of the Wales box, and rolls a weak curler into the arms of Ward. It’s all Portugal in terms of possession, but the hosts are holding their shape.
 Share 45m ago 15.20 EST 35 min: So having made the point about the Atari-game pace, the intensity drops markedly.
 Share 46m ago 15.19 EST 33 min: Davies nicks the ball off Fernandes, then immediately wins another 50-50 with Neves, who catches him late on the top of his boot. Neves should be booked, but the referee plays it cool. Don’t do it now and pay later.
 Share 48m ago 15.17 EST 31 min: … and now Thomas barrels down the left. He could shape a curler around Costa, but cuts back to tee up Wilson instead. A selfless act, but Wilson smashes his shot straight at Costa, who parries well. Wild end-to-end antics. The ball’s like a pixel in a game of Pong. Someone once wrote a song about that …
 Share 51m ago 15.15 EST 29 min: Brooks embarks on a power romp down the right. He’s got options, but takes a heavy touch. Portugal counter, Trincão advancing down the left. Trincão looks for Ramos in the middle, but Davies intercepts.
 Share 53m ago 15.13 EST 27 min: There’s another game going on in Group A4. “Hei!” begins Wil Lee-Wright. “While there might not be much to play for in the Wales-Portugal match, the Denmark Norway game is a match up for the ages. Norway need to win to leapfrog their neighbours, but they’ve not won a competitive game in the Danish capital in 100 years and despite a strong start, they’ve somehow conspired to find themselves 2-0 down after just 15 mins. Wil, from a despondent sports bar in Gjøvik, Norway.”
 Share 55m ago 15.11 EST 25 min: Roberts takes a quick throw from inside his own half to release James on the scamper down the right. He’s got team-mates in the middle, but his cross doesn’t beat the first man, so a corner will have to do. And from that, hit long from the right, Rodon slaps a poor header wide left from six yards. That’s another big chance spurned. In a parallel universe, it’s now 2-2.
 View image in fullscreen Wales' Joe Rodon rues his miss. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  15.27 EST 1h ago 15.09 EST 23 min: That should have been 1-2, and though the flag went up for offside, I’m not sure Trincão actually was. VAR might have reversed that decision had Trincão scored, as he surely should have. Let’s leave it be, for Trincão’s sake, there’s nothing to be gained from it.
 View image in fullscreen Portugal's Francisco Trincão shoots over the bar. Photograph: Alastair Grant/AP Share Updated at  15.14 EST 1h ago 15.07 EST 21 min: Neto glides in from the right, and curls a delicious cross towards Trincão, coming from the left to meet the ball six yards out. Trincão has to score, but leans back and volleys a quickly rising shot off the top of the crossbar and into the stand. What a miss!
 Share 1h ago 15.04 EST 19 min: Wales snaffle the ball and launch a fast counter. Wilson is close to barging free down the middle, only for Dalot to step in, just in time.
 Share 1h ago 15.03 EST 17 min: Cancelo is sent romping into acres down the right. His low cross isn’t all that, and Sheehan clears to great cheers. Sheehan now in moral credit.
 Share 1h ago 15.01 EST 16 min: Cancelo loops a long pass down the inside-right channel and nearly releases Neto. Ward comes to the edge of his box to claim. There are a few more goals in this.
 Share 1h ago 15.00 EST 14 min: VAR has a long check for an offside in the build-up … but all’s fine. That’s some reaction from Wales , and especially Sheehan, who has bounced back from his mistake with involvement in a goal.
 Share Updated at  15.03 EST 1h ago 14.59 EST GOAL! Wales 1-1 Portugal (Brooks 13)
 Oh yes! Yes they can! Sheehan sends Wilson free down the left. Wilson shoots. Costa parries. The ball pings back to Colwill, who rolls a pass towards Brooks on the penalty spot. Brooks sweeps into the bottom right, and that’s the perfect response!
 View image in fullscreen David Brooks gets Wales back on level terms with a sweet finish. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Brooks celebrates by blowing a kiss. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  15.10 EST 1h ago 14.57 EST 12 min: What a way to mark your 99th appearance. Can Wales respond?
 Share 1h ago 14.57 EST GOAL! Wales 0-1 Portugal (Fernandes 11)
 Er, scrub that. Sheehan, playing out from the back, is robbed by João Neves, who shuttles the ball infield for Fernandes, on the edge of the D. Fernandes whips a shot towards the top-left. Ward can’t reach it. What a finish, though from the Welsh point of view, that’s a self-inflicted wound.
 View image in fullscreen Portugal's Bruno Fernandes shoots to score the opening goal. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen And celebrates with a knee slide. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Share Updated at  15.13 EST 1h ago 14.55 EST 10 min: Nothing much going on at the moment.
 Share 1h ago 14.53 EST 8 min: Portugal stay patient, then suddenly go agricultural. A big hoof down the middle nearly releases Neto. Last man Dasilva does well to stand his ground and bat the ball away. “Some people make news even when they are not there - maybe more when they are not there,” begins krishnamoorthy v. “I want Portugal to win a few games resoundingly so that the team can discard the millstone and move on.”
 Share 1h ago 14.51 EST 6 min: Now it’s Ward’s turn to clank a poor pass straight to an opponent. Neto tries to release Cancelo into the Wales box with a wedge down the right, but gets it all wrong. Ward claims and breathes out again.
 Share 1h ago 14.49 EST 4 min: António Silva strides out of defence and scuffs a strange pass straight to James. He’s fortunate that James doesn’t seem to know what to do with the ball, even though he’s got a bit of time down the inside-right channel and Wilson in the middle. The ball’s handed straight back.
 Share 1h ago 14.47 EST 2 min: The atmosphere in the Cardiff City Stadium is more Fun than Excitement right now. Not a whole lot going on, and not that much riding on it either.
 Share 1h ago 14.46 EST Wales get the ball rolling. James hares after a long pass down the left but can’t get past Dalot. A positive start, though.
 Share 1h ago 14.42 EST The teams are out! Wales in red, Portugal in second-choice white and green. Bruno Fernandes stands in line for the Portuguese national anthem for the 99th time. Once the day is done, he’ll be just the 135 caps shy of Cristiano Ronaldo’s record. We’ll be off in a minute!
 View image in fullscreen Gone, but not forgotten. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters Share Updated at  15.23 EST 1h ago 14.38 EST Bellamy’s on the Beeb now, where he’s heaping praise on Portugal . “A good team … really good … in that team there’s seven European Cups between them … so they’re strong … talent … if you look at Vitinha and Neves, they’re probably my two favourite players at this present moment … we have to put the shackles on them … the best form of defence is to attack.”
 Share 2h ago 14.29 EST Craig Bellamy speaks to S4C. “[Portugal] can score four or five as well [as Denmark] …on the day they were quite unlucky … the opportunities they created … they didn’t convert them … we’re aware of their threat … at times they will be open as well … even when we’re suffering, there’s always an opportunity to exploit the space … no doubt we can impose our game … now we want the results … tonight that’s the aim … can we make them suffer? … it’s a tough test … but an exciting one as well.”
 Share 2h ago 13.52 EST Portugal make four changes after that 4-1 defeat at home to Denmark. Rúben Dias is suspended so António Silva comes into the defence. João Neves, João Cancelo and Francisco Trincão step up; João Félix, Alberto Costa and Rúben Neves sit down. The Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs is also on the bench, sporting Portugal’s fancy new post-Cristiano continental-style No 7.
 Portugal immortalise Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt in tribute to national legend Read more Share 2h ago 13.42 EST Wales make six changes to their starting line-up following the 3-1 defeat in Norway. Two are enforced: Ethan Ampadu is suspended while Neco Williams is injured. In come Danny Ward, David Brooks, Connor Roberts, Rubin Colwill, Sorba Thomas and Josh Sheehan. Karl Darlow, Liam Cullen, Lewis Koumas and Brennan Johnson drop to the bench.
 Norway 3-1 Wales: Nations League – as it happened Read more Share 3h ago 13.34 EST The teams
 Wales: Ward, Roberts, Rodon, B Davies, Dasilva, Wilson, Sheehan, Brooks, D James, R Colwill, Thomas.
 Portugal: Costa, Dalot, Silva, Veiga, Cancelo, Vitinha, Fernandes, Neto, Trincao, Ramos, Neves.
 Referee: Sven Jablonski (Germany) 
 Share Updated at  13.54 EST 3h ago 13.30 EST Preamble
 This is a free hit for Wales . Craig Bellamy and his men have nothing to worry about, because despite being guaranteed to finish bottom of Group A4, as a result of the old head-to-head rule …
 1. Portugal P5 W4 D0 L1 GD+2 Pts 12
2. Denmark P5 W3 D0 L2 GD+3 Pts 9
3. Norway P5 W2 D0 L3 GD0 Pts 6
4. Wales P5 W1 D0 L4 GD-5 Pts 3 
 … they’re also guaranteed to finish top of the ranking of League A’s fourth-placed teams …
 1. Wales (A4) P5 W1 D0 L4 GD-5 Pts 3
2. Serbia (A2) P6 W0 D0 L6 GD-8 Pts 0
3. Turkey (A1) P6 W0 D0 L6 GD-11 Pts 0
4. Czechia (A3) P6 W0 D0 L6 GD-11 Pts 0 
 … and so this Byzantine journey will lead them to a relegation/promotion play-off with some of the runners-up in League B. But that’s a concern for March; this is now! Can Wales bounce back after their spirited defeat in Norway ? Will Portugal prove a point after their humbling by Denmark , the first misstep in the post-Him world? Kick-off is at 7.45pm. It’s on!
